questions.question: Ch13 Q41. In the Green Mart Balanced Scorecard example, the Financial Perspective target includes: EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 112 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: Maintaining a customer satisfaction rating of at least 4 out of 5
Achieving a 10% increase in sales revenue and maintaining a net profit margin of 8%
Increasing inventory turnover by 20% and reducing carbon emissions by 15%
Increasing employee training hours by 25%
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q42. In the Green Mart Balanced Scorecard example, the Internal Business Processes Perspective measures include:
options: Employee training hours and number of new product ideas
Total sales revenue and net profit margin
Inventory turnover rate and carbon footprint reduction
Customer satisfaction scores and repeat purchase rate
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q43. "Strategy Mapping" was developed by Kaplan and Norton as:
options: A replacement for the Balanced Scorecard in complex organizations
An extension to the Balanced Scorecard to make implementations more successful — showing cause-and-effect relationships between objectives
A financial analysis technique for comparing departmental budgets
A standalone strategic planning tool independent of the Balanced Scorecard
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q44. A key problem with the Balanced Scorecard identified in the chapter is that:
options: Many employees do not understand the organization's strategy and systems such as performance management are not linked to the strategy
It focuses too heavily on non-financial measures at the expense of profitability
It requires too many external benchmarks to be effective
It is only applicable to manufacturing organizations and not service firms
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q45. The Balanced Scorecard helps reduce the tendency to:
options: Focus on a broad range of measures simultaneously
Align internal processes with external customer requirements
Concentrate on one measure — broadening the manager's view of performance
Develop long-term strategic objectives for the organization
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q46. Gains in one Balanced Scorecard perspective need to be considered alongside:
options: Government regulations and compliance requirements
Only the customer perspective to maintain competitive advantage
Losses that may arise in other perspectives — encouraging a holistic view
Only the financial perspective regardless of other outcomes
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q47. The main reason for the creation of Multidimensional Performance Models is:
options: Traditional financial performance systems have moved from being a performance system more to an information system aimed at satisfying external stakeholders — poorly designed to guide organizational direction EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 113 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
Government regulations now require multidimensional reporting from all organizations
Financial measures have become too complex for managers to understand
Non-financial measures have proven to be more accurate than financial measures
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q48. A key criticism of traditional performance systems is that managers have learned to:
options: Manage the traditional performance systems to obtain numbers that meet goals and secure bonuses — rather than managing the business itself
Rely entirely on external benchmarks rather than internal performance data
Set overly ambitious targets to attract investor interest
Ignore financial targets and focus on non-financial outcomes
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q49. Advances in technology have paradoxically created which problem for performance measurement?
options: An overload of information — vital information gets lost among excessive data
Reduced data collection capabilities across organizations
Inability to process complex financial calculations in real time
Reduced accuracy in financial reporting and ratio analysis
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q50. Service businesses face a fundamental challenge in measuring performance because:
options: Their customers, activities, and deals vary too widely — and people bring unpredictable differences in experience, skills, and motivation
They are prohibited from using external benchmarks for comparison
Their production processes are identical to manufacturing firms
They have no financial costs that need to be measured or controlled
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q51. The FIRST principle of service measurement states that service companies should:
options: Outsource all measurement activities to specialist consultancies
Compare themselves against their own performance — rather than against poorly defined external measures
Focus primarily on comparing against external industry benchmarks
Use only financial costs to measure performance variance
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q52. The SECOND principle of service measurement states that service companies must:
options: Look deeper than their financial costs to discover and monitor the root causes of those expenses
Focus only on top-level financial costs to keep analysis simple
Restrict measurement to quantitative metrics and avoid qualitative data
Compare their performance against the top three competitors in their industry
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q53. The THIRD principle of service measurement states that service companies must:
options: Focus all measurement on individual employee productivity
Restrict measurement to a single functional area to avoid complexity
Set up broad cost-measurement systems to report and compare all expenses across functional silos — improving understanding of cross-functional trade-offs
Replace all internal measurement with external benchmarking
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q54. Why is variance particularly difficult to measure in service businesses? EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 114 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: Service businesses are too small to afford sophisticated measurement systems
Service businesses are not required to measure performance by law
Service activities are identical across all locations making comparison unnecessary
Metrics are not uniform across business units — for example one group in a call center may regard all calls on a given issue as a single case while another logs every call separately
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q55. "Service-level agreements" create measurement challenges because:
options: They eliminate the need for performance measurement in service firms
The more types of services a business offers, the more variability it can expect in its agreements
They require only financial metrics to assess compliance
They are always identical across all customer types and service lines
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q56. "Internal benchmarks" are recommended over "external benchmarks" for service companies because:
options: Internal benchmarks deliver more detailed metrics — allowing a company to find its own best practices and understand true cost drivers with full access to relevant information
External benchmarks always lead to overestimation of performance variance
External benchmarks are always more accurate than internal data
Government regulations prohibit the use of external benchmarks in service firms
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q57. A "Cost Tree with Detailed Metrics" is described as:
options: A financial statement showing total organizational expenditure
A government-required reporting format for service companies
A marketing tool for analyzing the profitability of different customer segments

An important tool to help companies define internal benchmarks — allowing managers to compare performance of different accounts against similar metrics and calculate which improvements will have the most impact
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q58. "Measure Cost Drivers" as a principle of service measurement means:
options: Comparing service costs against the industry average benchmark
Measuring only the top-level financial costs of service delivery
Outsourcing all cost analysis to specialist financial consultants
Looking at the underlying cause of each expense — such as cost per employee, incidents per employee per day, or incidents per product — rather than just the total cost
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q59. "Measure Deep and Broad" as a principle of service measurement means:
options: Focusing measurement on a single key cost area to maximize precision
Taking a comprehensive approach — measuring all relevant costs rather than only selected costs — because services are fungible and it is easy to shift costs to unmeasured areas
Using only external benchmarks to ensure objectivity
Restricting measurement to financial costs only
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q60. The Performance Pyramid was developed by:
options: Fitzgerald and Moon in the 1990s
Kaplan and Norton in 1992
Lynch and Cross as a model to understand and define the links between objectives and performance measures at different levels in the organization
Porter and Miles as an extension of the competitive strategy framework
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q61. The Performance Pyramid is designed to ensure that:
options: Performance measurement is restricted to the top two levels of the organization
The activities of every department, system, and business unit support the overall vision of the organization
Financial measures take precedence over non-financial measures at all levels
Only senior management is responsible for setting performance targets
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q62. At the TOP of the Performance Pyramid is:
options: Business operating system measures of internal processes
Day-to-day operational measures
Business unit critical success factors in terms of market and financial measures
The Vision — through which the organization describes how it will achieve long-term success and competitive advantage
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q63. The SECOND level of the Performance Pyramid — the Business Unit — includes:
options: The overall vision and long-term competitive strategy
Critical success factors in terms of market-related measures and financial measures
Day-to-day operational measures of productivity and quality
Internal systems and processes needed to meet customer needs
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q64. The THIRD level of the Performance Pyramid — Business Operating Systems — includes:
options: The overall organizational vision and mission
Measures relating to internal systems and processes needed to meet the needs of customers — such as flexibility measures showing responsiveness to customer demands
Day-to-day operational measures at the shop-floor level
Critical success factors in terms of market share and financial returns
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q65. The LOWEST level of the Performance Pyramid contains:
options: The organizational vision and long-term competitive strategy
Day-to-day operational measures
Internal process measures and operational flexibility metrics
Business unit critical success factors and financial targets
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q66. In the Performance Pyramid, objectives flow in which direction?
options: In both directions simultaneously at all levels
Downward — cascading from the vision through to operational measures
From the left side of the pyramid to the right side
From the bottom of the pyramid upward to the vision
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q67. In the Performance Pyramid, measures and information flow in which direction? EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 116 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
options: From the left side to the right side at each level
From the bottom upward — operational measures inform higher-level performance
Downward from the vision to operational measures
From right to left — from financial to non-financial
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q68. The LEFT-hand side of the Performance Pyramid contains measures which are:
options: Predominantly financial and internally focused
Strategic-level measures linked only to shareholder returns
Day-to-day operational measures only
Predominantly non-financial and externally focused
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q69. The RIGHT-hand side of the Performance Pyramid contains measures which are:
options: Related to innovation and employee development
Focused on the internal efficiency of the organization and predominantly financial
Related to customer satisfaction and market share
Externally focused and non-financial
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q70. A limitation of the Performance Pyramid identified in the chapter is that it:
options: Focuses too heavily on financial measures at all levels
Is too complex and hierarchical for practical implementation in service firms
Does not include any non-financial measures of performance
Tends to concentrate on only two groups of stakeholders — shareholders and customers — making it necessary to ensure measures for other stakeholders are also included
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q71. CIMA's official definition of Performance Measurement describes it as:
options: A human resource tool for evaluating individual employee performance
A financial reporting tool for satisfying external stakeholder requirements
A marketing tool for measuring customer satisfaction and brand equity
The process of assessing the proficiency with which a reporting entity succeeds — by the economic acquisition of resources and their efficient and effective deployment — in achieving its objectives
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q72. Which of the following is identified as a reason why setting performance measures is "often more difficult than would first be imagined"?
options: Government regulations restrict the types of measures organizations can use
Employees always resist the introduction of new performance measurement systems
Improving one objective — such as hospital waiting times — can have a negative effect on another equally important objective — such as quality of healthcare
Performance measures are too expensive for small organizations to implement
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option C

questions.question: Ch13 Q73. The link between CSFs and performance measurement ensures that:
options: The performance measurement system ties into the overall strategy — areas where results must be satisfactory for competitive success are measured and monitored EM MCQ BANK Chapter 13: Performance Measurement Tools Page 117 Complete MCQ Reference All Chapters Included
All departments use identical performance measures regardless of strategic priorities
Only financial CSFs are translated into measurable KPIs
Performance measures are set exclusively by external consultants
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option A

questions.question: Ch13 Q74. KPIs for the CSF of "efficient production" in a cost leadership strategy could include:
options: Employee engagement levels and training hours
Maximum kg of materials wasted and average time taken to produce one unit
Market share growth and brand awareness scores
Customer satisfaction scores and repeat purchase rates
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q75. Once a performance measurement system is implemented, management must ensure that:
options: Only senior management has access to performance data
Performance measures are reviewed only at the annual board meeting
The system remains identical regardless of changes in the business environment
Information systems are put in place to collect data allowing performance to be measured on an ongoing basis
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option D

questions.question: Ch13 Q76. Which of the following correctly identifies the FOUR perspectives of the Balanced Scorecard with an appropriate example measure?
options: Financial — market share; Customer — carbon footprint; Internal — revenue growth; Learning — repeat purchase rate
Financial — employee training hours; Customer — net profit margin; Internal — customer satisfaction; Learning — inventory turnover
Financial — total sales revenue; Customer — customer satisfaction scores; Internal — inventory turnover rate; Learning — employee training hours
Financial — customer loyalty; Customer — profit margin; Internal — training hours; Learning — stock price

questions.question: Ch13 Q77. Which building block of Fitzgerald and Moon's model ensures employees are motivated to achieve standards?

Rewards — by linking clear and desirable incentives to standard achievement
All three building blocks equally — no single block is more important
Dimensions — by providing clear goals for the business
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q78. Which of the following BEST explains why multidimensional performance models were created?
options: Technology limitations prevented accurate financial data collection

Traditional financial systems were designed primarily to satisfy external stakeholders and poorly designed to guide internal organizational direction — while managers learned to manage the numbers rather than the business
Government regulations required organizations to adopt non-financial reporting
Traditional financial systems were too expensive to maintain
questions.explanation: Correct option according to Answer Key is Option B

questions.question: Ch13 Q79. In CIMA's terminology, "economic acquisition of resources" as part of performance measurement refers to:
options: Eliminating all non-essential resources from the production process EM MCQ BANK
Purchasing resources exclusively from domestic suppliers
Maximizing production output regardless of resource cost
Acquiring resources at minimum cost — the efficiency of resource procurement

questions.question: Ch13 Q80. Which of the following statements about the Balanced Scorecard is TRUE?
options: It focuses exclusively on internal operational efficiency
It brings together a wide range of financial and non-financial measures to give managers a broader perspective — ensuring gains in one area are considered alongside losses in other areas
It is only applicable to large multinational corporations with complex operations
It was designed to replace all existing financial performance measures
